predecessors.note: The Ikkō-ikki page dates the rebellion to 1486; the Sengoku page to 1488.

land.text: Kaga Province, 'conquered by Oda Nobunaga's general Shibata Katsuie'

successors.note: The Kaga Province page gives no year for the conquest; 1580 is the year the Ikkō-ikki surrendered Ishiyama Hongan-ji (Sengoku and Azuchi-Momoyama pages).

capitals.name: Kanazawa area (map anchor; the ikki's own seat is not named on the pages opened)
capitals.note: Ikkō-ikki infobox: capital 'Ishiyama Hongan-ji (de facto, 1496-1580)', the movement's centre in Osaka; none of the pages opened names the seat of the Kaga ikki itself.

correction.text: the entire province of Kaga, the area the Kaga ikki 'assumed control of' and kept for nearly 100 years

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks (its Warring States Japan row draws the whole archipelago as one shape). Kaga Province is 'today the south and western portion of Ishikawa Prefecture' (Kaga Province page); the region is approximated by the part of Ishikawa within 50 km of Kanazawa, which also takes in the southern edge of Noto. No page gives an area.

ledger.note: 1488: the Kaga Rebellion makes the Kaga ikki master of Kaga. Sengoku timeline: the Kaga Rebellion establishes the Kaga ikki, which 'assumed control of the entire province of Kaga'; the page says it remained independent for nearly 100 years. The Ikkō-ikki page dates the rebellion to 1486 ('overthrew the governor of Kaga Province and established self-rule'): 'the first time in Japanese history that a group of commoners ruled a province'. The Kaga Province page calls it 'a loosely governed confederation'.

region.text: the entire province of Kaga, conquered by Shibata Katsuie

ledger.note: 1580: Oda power ends the Kaga ikki. The Kaga Province page says only that 'The area was eventually conquered by Oda Nobunaga's general Shibata Katsuie', with no year; 1580 is the year the Sengoku and Azuchi-Momoyama pages give for the Ikkō-ikki finally surrendering Ishiyama Hongan-ji after an 11-year siege. Page silent on Kaga's own year; the Ikkō-ikki infobox gives 'Disestablished 1586' for the movement as a whole.

wars.name: Kaga Rebellion
wars.outcome: The ikki overthrew the governor and took the province; Kaga stayed self-ruled for nearly 100 years.

wars.name: Ishiyama Hongan-ji War

zones.text: Kaga Province, the Ikkō-ikki's province, conquered by Shibata Katsuie

wars.outcome: Oda took Ishiyama Hongan-ji 'in 1580 after an 11-year siege'; the Kaga Province page has Kaga conquered by Shibata Katsuie, undated.
wars.note: The Sengoku page's timeline dates the start to 1570 ('Battle of Anegawa and the beginning of the Ishiyama Hongan-ji War'); the Ikkō-ikki page's '11-year siege' ending 1580 would count back to 1569. Start corrected from 1569 to 1570 by the jk-01-c reviewer, 2026-10-18.

certainty.note: A province held by a confederation of commoners and Hongan-ji followers, with no treaty or survey line; its edge is the old provincial border, approximated here.

notes:
Written by Phase B agent jk-01-c on 2026-10-18 as a rebel state added for rule 5 (the one warring-states-japan loses to, 1488-1580); it uses the four pages already opened for warring-states-japan (Sengoku period, Ikkō-ikki, Kaga Province, Azuchi-Momoyama period) and no others.

Not settled: the start year (Sengoku page 1488, Ikkō-ikki page 1486), the end year (1580 inferred from the fall of Ishiyama Hongan-ji; the Kaga Province page names Shibata Katsuie without a year), the seat of the ikki (no page opened names it), the exact extent (Kaga Province is not a gazetteer entry: a 50 km circle at Kanazawa within Ishikawa stands in for it) and Wikidata (no id from a page). The Ikkō-ikki also held Echizen's Yoshizaki (founded 1471), Nagashima (destroyed by 1574) and Mikawa (defeated at Azukizaki in 1564) for shorter times and the Yamashiro ikki (1485) and Iga ikki (1477-1581) are on the Sengoku table; none of these is recorded because the pages give no extent or end for them.
